meeting_header: Date: 2025-02-14 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Ibrahim Khan (Redwood SE), Rita Chen (Redwood CSM); Sarah Lee (Acme Head of Security), Daniel Ortiz (Platform Eng), Maria Gomez (IT Ops), Kevin Wu (Compliance)
summary: Security review focused on SSO/SAML/SCIM integration and RBAC model. Discussed least-privilege roles, SCIM group sync cadence, audit log retention and schema, KMS usage and customer-managed keys, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, and timeline for pilot. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send metadata and guides, Acme to share pilot users, schedule follow-up RBAC walkthrough and staging test.
topics: SSO/SAML setup and SP/IdP metadata exchange
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
transcript: [00:00] Lena Park: hi everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off the security review for SSO and RBAC at Acme
[00:12] Sarah Lee: hey lena thanks, quick note — we have Kevin from compliance and Daniel from platform, Maria's on for ops
[00:20] Ibrahim Khan: morning all, Ibrahim from Redwood infra team, I'll cover the technical bits like SCIM and KMS
[00:32] Maria Gomez: hey, just to flag our timeline we want pilot in staging by end of month if possible
[00:45] Lena Park: yes that's the goal, we'll try to keep it tight — first we'll talk about SAML config and SCIM mapping
[00:58] Daniel Ortiz: quick question, do you support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows? we use IdP-initiated most of the time
[01:05] Ibrahim Khan: we support both, SP and IdP initiation; we'll provide SP metadata and endpoints. sometimes the auto-generated metadata has minor differences depending on provider
[01:22] Sarah Lee: ok; we use Azure AD but some teams use Okta; we need a single integration path ideally
[01:30] Ibrahim Khan: that's fine. Azure AD and Okta are first-class; we have seen the SAML attribute names vary — email vs userPrincipalName — we'll include attribute mapping guidance
[01:46] Kevin Wu: about SCIM — does Redwood support group sync and delta sync? we don't want full re-provision daily

[01:55] Ibrahim Khan: yes SCIM supports incremental push (PATCH/PUT) and we recommend group-based provisioning. delta diffs are supported; our default sync cadence is configurable — you can set 5m, 15m, 60m depending on load
[02:12] Daniel Ortiz: what's the expected rate limit on SCIM? if we have thousands of users we need throughput numbers
[02:20] Ibrahim Khan: good point — default throttles are 600 calls per minute for SCIM, but for Dedicated/private deploys we can increase that. we'll document exact quotas in the guide
[02:36] Maria Gomez: and user deprovisioning needs to be immediate for terminated employees — how fast does it remove access?

[02:45] Ibrahim Khan: deprovisioning is near real-time once the SCIM PATCH hits us; the token/session invalidation depends — we support session revocation via API and short-lived session tokens can be enforced via RBAC policies
[03:00] Sarah Lee: let's talk RBAC — we want least-privilege, separate dev vs prod roles, and auditability
[03:10] Lena Park: yes we recommend roles: Admin (account-level), Operator (deploy/manage), Viewer (read-only), and a Billing-only role if you need. we can map these to SCIM groups
[03:25] Daniel Ortiz: can we customize permissions granularly? e.g., allow model deployment but not access to audit logs
[03:33] Ibrahim Khan: currently permissions are resource-scoped: you can grant model:deploy, model:invoke, logs:view, billing:view etc. we can do custom role composition for Enterprise customers
[03:48] Sarah Lee: who normally manages the RBAC roles? we want separation: security team defines roles, platform team applies them
[03:57] Lena Park: that's common — security defines policy and platform uses SCIM to provision mapping. we recommend a review workflow where changes require a second approver
[04:12] Kevin Wu: on audit logs — what events are logged and how long do you retain them? we need 1 year for compliance

[04:22] Ibrahim Khan: logs include auth events (SAML/SP/IdP), provisioning events (SCIM create/modify/delete), admin actions (role grants, model rollouts), and API calls. default retention is 90 days, but for enterprise we can extend to 1 year or ship to customer SIEM (via streaming or S3 exports)
[04:45] Sarah Lee: good — can we get a sample schema of the audit log? we need field names and examples for our ingestion
[04:52] Ibrahim Khan: yes we'll share the audit log schema JSON; note sometimes field names can be slightly different in exports, we'll annotate them
[05:05] Daniel Ortiz: about encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? we can't have provider-managed keys for prod data
[05:13] Ibrahim Khan: yes for Private deployments we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted API we offer CMK via cloud KMS in dedicated accounts; we can discuss key rotation policies too
[05:29] Maria Gomez: is data encrypted at rest end-to-end? and what about envelope encryption for embeddings?

[05:37] Ibrahim Khan: all persisted data is encrypted at rest. for extra control we use envelope encryption with CMK to wrap data keys; embeddings are treated as customer data and follow same encryption path
[05:50] Sarah Lee: data residency — we need data to stay in eu-west-1 for EU customers. how do you guarantee that?

[05:58] Lena Park: we have region controls and can pin deployments to specific regions; for Private you can run in your VPC; for Hosted we route by region and can restrict cross-region backups on enterprise contracts
[06:12] Kevin Wu: SOC 2 — can you share your Type II report? also ISO certificate?
[06:18] Rita Chen: yes we'll share links and a read-only portal for the artifacts. some docs are NDA gated; we'll give access once the paperwork is done
[06:30] Sarah Lee: good. one more on SAML — when the SP metadata is provided, what attributes should we expect to receive for role mapping?
[06:40] Ibrahim Khan: typically we map groups via the 'memberOf' or 'groups' SAML attribute. email or sub as principal. we'll provide sample attribute mapping for Azure AD and Okta
[06:55] Daniel Ortiz: do you support SCIM group custom attributes? we tag groups with environment:prod/dev
[07:03] Ibrahim Khan: yes custom group attributes are supported; SCIM supports extension schemas and we can map them into RBAC labels
[07:20] Maria Gomez: about session lifetime — can we enforce SSO session limit to 8 hours?
[07:27] Ibrahim Khan: session TTL is configurable; for Hosted we default 24h, but you can set shorter TTLs with forced re-auth or immediate revocation on deprovisioning
[07:40] Sarah Lee: is there support for SAML artifact binding? one of our vendors uses it
[07:47] Ibrahim Khan: we primarily use POST and Redirect bindings; artifact binding is less common and might require additional configuration — we can check compatibility
[07:58] Lena Park: hey, quick interruption — some of our docs refer to 'Redwood dedicate' in one place, that's a typo, should be 'Redwood Dedicated' — apologies for the transcribe glitch
[08:10] Sarah Lee: no worries, we had similar typos in our internal docs too
[08:20] Kevin Wu: audit integrity — do logs have tamper-evidence? we need cryptographic integrity for some events
[08:27] Ibrahim Khan: we can stream logs to customer-controlled S3 or to a SIEM where you can apply immutability policies. for extra assurance we support signed log bundles on request
[08:40] Daniel Ortiz: what's the change-control process for RBAC changes? we want approval workflows and history
[08:48] Lena Park: actions are logged; for Enterprise we can integrate with ticketing to require MR approval. changes show up in audit logs with actor info and timestamps
[09:00] Maria Gomez: talk me through the SCIM initial provision: we create groups in IdP, map to roles, then Redwood provisions users into appropriate teams?

[09:10] Ibrahim Khan: yes flow is: create groups in IdP -> SCIM push groups/users -> Redwood maps groups to roles -> provisioned users get role-based entitlements. during pilot we recommend a small set of pilot groups and test accounts
[09:26] Daniel Ortiz: will group renames break mappings?
[09:31] Ibrahim Khan: we map by immutable group id when possible; name changes are handled but best practice is to avoid renames during early syncs
[09:44] Sarah Lee: regarding least privilege — can we have a 'Model Reader' role that can see model configs but not run them?
[09:52] Ibrahim Khan: yes we can create that: model:read, model:config:view but not model:invoke
[10:05] Lena Park: i'll note that as a requested custom role in the action items
[10:12] Sarah Lee: about account recovery and break-glass — if SSO is misconfigured how do admins regain access?
[10:20] Ibrahim Khan: we support emergency local admin accounts for break-glass which can be enabled via a verified process — we log those events and require justification
[10:35] Kevin Wu: what's the process for key compromise? if a CMK is suspected compromised what's recovery and rotation look like?

[10:43] Ibrahim Khan: rotate data encryption keys and re-wrap; for CMK compromise you rotate the CMK and re-encrypt affected data keys. timeline depends on dataset size; we have playbooks for rotation and can help with assisted ops
[10:56] Daniel Ortiz: any limits on the number of roles or groups? we have complex org with many teams
[11:03] Ibrahim Khan: platform can scale to thousands of groups; performance tuning may be needed for very large orgs. Dedicated/private gives more headroom
[11:17] Maria Gomez: can we get a sample RBAC mapping template?
[11:22] Lena Park: yes, we'll share the spreadsheet template and fill a sample mapping with you
[11:30] Sarah Lee: also need logging for admin console access — who clicked what in the console
[11:38] Ibrahim Khan: that's part of admin audit events — console UI actions are captured. we include target resource, actor, action, timestamp, and IP
[11:52] Daniel Ortiz: IP addresses — are they stored in logs? any PII concerns?
[11:59] Ibrahim Khan: IPs are logged; in EU deployments we can pseudonymize or hash IPs if required for privacy compliance
[12:12] Sarah Lee: regulatory question — for some regulated workloads we need on-prem; does Redwood offer air-gapped installs?
[12:20] Lena Park: yes Private has on-prem package and air-gapped option. that includes local KMS/HSM and no data egress to Redwood control plane if requested
[12:35] Kevin Wu: curious about encryption in transit — mutual TLS?
[12:41] Ibrahim Khan: mutual TLS is supported for service-to-service; user-facing traffic uses TLS1.2/1.3 with HSTS. for Private deployments we can enable mTLS for internal endpoints
[12:55] Maria Gomez: what about retention policies for embeddings vs logs vs raw request payloads? we treat embeddings as customer data but do you store raw prompts?

[13:04] Ibrahim Khan: default behavior is store prompts and outputs for X days for debugging, but with enterprise retention you can configure or disable retention. embeddings are stored according to data retention policy — we can set separate TTLs
[13:20] Sarah Lee: okay good. next steps — can you walk through what's needed from our side to start the pilot?
[13:28] Lena Park: we'll need: SAML IdP metadata, list of pilot users/groups, confirmation of desired RBAC roles, and whether you'll use CMK. Rita will share SOC2 docs
[13:40] Daniel Ortiz: i'll prepare pilot users and groups. also i'll want Ibrahim to join for configuration in staging
[13:47] Ibrahim Khan: happy to join — i can do the SCIM connect and SAML test with Daniel
[13:55] Sarah Lee: one more — can you provide a sample service-account pattern for automation that doesn't require human SSO?
[14:03] Ibrahim Khan: yes we support service tokens with scoping; service accounts can be created and pinned to roles, and those tokens are audited and rotateable
[14:18] Daniel Ortiz: token TTLs and rotation cadence? we prefer short lived with automated rotation
[14:25] Ibrahim Khan: service tokens default 24h TTL but can be shorter; we integrate with your secret manager for rotation automation
[14:40] Kevin Wu: ok compliance will review SOC2 artifacts once provided; Kevin will follow up on specific control mappings
[14:48] Kevin Wu: (speaking) one ask — we need evidence for change management controls around key rotations and role changes
[14:55] Rita Chen: we'll include change management playbooks and examples in the artifact pack
[15:02] Sarah Lee: anything else on RBAC customization or SCIM?
[15:08] Daniel Ortiz: curious about onboarding existing users — can we sync historical activity?
[15:15] Ibrahim Khan: activity is not backfilled into Redwood logs; you can ingest external historical logs into your SIEM and correlate, but platform logs start at integration time

[15:26] Lena Park: wrapping up — agreed actions and timeline. lena to send SAML metadata and integration docs, ibrahim to prepare RBAC mapping, daniel to send pilot users, rita to share SOC2/ISO links
[15:40] Sarah Lee: thanks everyone, we'll target staging pilot next week.
[15:46] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for RBAC walkthrough
[15:52] (call ends)
